🇺🇦 Apartment sales in Kiev’s new-build market have collapsed tenfold compared with 2021, according to Ukrainian media. Citing Igor Raikov, founder of the Kiev School of Development, Ukrainian media report that monthly sales of newly built apartments in the capital have fallen to just $20 million. That compares with approximately $200 million in September 2021 and $38.4 million in August this year. Several factors are putting potential buyers off, including power outages, Russian strikes, exchange-rate fluctuations and limited access to government housing programmes. The downturn has left Kiev developers sitting on an estimated 17,000 unsold apartments. At the current rate of sales, it could take more than eight years to clear the existing inventory. A stark indication of the pressure facing Ukraine’s property market. 🔴 @DDGeopolitics

European countries’ unwillingness to discuss a new regional security architecture is a bad look for them, Leonid Slutsky, leader of Russia’s Liberal Democratic Party and member of the State Duma Committee on International Affairs, said. “European representatives’ refusal to engage in constructive discussions on establishing a new non-NATO-centered regional security architecture looks like a clear sign of the European Union’s deepening decline,” he wrote in an op-ed for TASS. “While Russian and US negotiators are working to find a diplomatic solution to the Ukraine conflict, European capitals appear to be sinking deeper and deeper into their political schizophrenia,” Slutsky noted.
